title: Parallel I-O
body:
[[Asynchronous Handshaking]]

Parallel I/O moves a whole word at once, one wire per bit, plus control lines. The
printer port is the classic example.

Faster than [[Serial I-O]] per transfer, but it costs a wire per bit, and at high speeds
the bits stop arriving together: small differences in wire length and capacitance mean
*skew*, and the receiver has to wait for the slowest line. That is why fast modern links
went back to serial.

With no clock shared between the two ends, coordination is done with
[[Asynchronous Handshaking]].
